issues.failure_explanation: The theorems' O hides Γ, built from C_o, C_s, C_f, C_g. These contain c_0 ∋ 4σ^2, C_f=(1+c_0)^3/(4L) and C_g ∋ 4σ^2, so Γ grows like a high power of σ. The 'deterministic' term Γ/√T and the factor Γ^{1/2} multiplying σ^{1/2}T^{-1/4} therefore scale polynomially in σ. The bound is not of the advertised noise-adaptive form T^{-1/2}+σ^{1/2}T^{-1/4} with σ-free constants.

issues.failure_explanation: In OptEMA-M, α_t=ρ_t^{-1/2} depends on ||g_t||^2. Both z_t, through (1-α_t), and α_t are correlated with the noise g_t-∇f(x_t). The cross term E<z_t, α_t(g_t-∇f(x_t))> need not vanish. Likewise, E[α_t^2||g_t-∇f||^2] ≤ α_t^2 E||g_t||^2 pulls a random factor out of the expectation and uses an inequality that holds only on average.

issues.failure_explanation: Several steps treat expectations as pathwise quantities. (i) E[max(X,Y)] ≤ max(EX,EY) is false; it is used for ||m_t||^2 and for max_t||s_t||^2 after summation by parts. (ii) From E[Σα_t||s_t||^2] ≤ K one cannot conclude E[Σ||s_t||^2] ≤ E[K/α_T], because α_T is random. (iii) Lemma G:bound only bounds E||g_t||^2, yet τ_T=max||g_i|| and ||g_t||^2 are bounded pathwise. Under bounded variance, τ_T is not bounded almost surely.
